Capitol Records, from December 1963 when it began issuing Beatles recordings for the US market, exercised complete control over format,[[90]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewisohn1992350-92) compiling distinct US albums from the band's recordings and issuing songs of their choosing as singles.[[174]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGould2007295–296-180)[[nb 7]](#cite_note-182) In June 1966, the Capitol LP *[Yesterday and Today](/wiki/Yesterday_and_Today "Yesterday and Today")* caused an uproar with its cover, which portrayed the grinning Beatles dressed in butcher's overalls, accompanied by raw meat and mutilated plastic baby dolls. According to Beatles biographer [Bill Harry](/wiki/Bill_Harry "Bill Harry"), it has been incorrectly suggested that this was meant as a satirical response to the way Capitol had "butchered" the US versions of the band's albums.[[176]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarry2000a1187-183) Thousands of copies of the LP had a new cover pasted over the original; an unpeeled "first-state" copy fetched $10,500 at a December 2005 auction.[[177]](#cite_note-184) In England, meanwhile, Harrison met sitar maestro [Ravi Shankar](/wiki/Ravi_Shankar "Ravi Shankar"), who agreed to train him on the instrument.[[178]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELavezzoli2006176-185)

Unlike typical Cursed Corpses, Panda possesses three interchangeable cores that alter his form and abilities between panda, gorilla, and triceratops modes. During the Sister School Exchange Event, he befriends Mechamaru after their match. Following Yaga's death, Panda participates in the Culling Games alongside Yuji and Megumi. The damage reduces Panda to a smaller, cub-like form, though he survives the encounter.
